sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2002. The Central and Southern Loloish Languages of Vietnam. Proceedings of the 28th Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society: Special Session on Tibeto-Burman and Southeast Asian Linguistics, pp. 1-13. doi:10.3765/bls.v28i2.1042
sources.note: Sec. 4 'Lahu' (Viet Black Lahu of Muong Te, autonym Khucong [khu tsho]), p.7: gives only initials, vowels and 'The seven tones for Vietnam Black Lahu are 33, 35, 53, 31, 212, 53ʔ and 31ʔ'; p.8 lexical comparison China Kucong vs Viet Kucong citing Sun 1992. Nothing on stress/accent for Lahu/Kucong (the 'iambic.. first syllable often unstressed' remarks on pp.3,5 are about Coong, not Kucong).
